entities.title: One implementation per operation, the daemon's where both had one
entities.summary: shell-tools became a library of the daemon; walking, searching and outlining use the daemon's walk cache, find scan and language-module outlines, and shell-tools keeps the JSON protocol, session memory, stat and diff_since.
entities.context: shell-tools and the daemon each walked, searched, listed, outlined, read and remembered what a session had seen. The owner asked to turn shell-tools into a library the daemon includes, merging their implementations, and to decide on evidence. Benchmarks on 2026-11-19 (Linux VM, 4 cores, 15 GiB, warm page cache), one process linking both crates, over ~/.cargo/registry/src (18,432 files, 786 MB) and src/macos/daemon (181 files): walk - the daemon's validated walk cache 72-84 ms cold and 5-9 ms warm, shell-tools' walk 85-145 ms on every search; search, 19 different patterns after a warm-up - daemon find 81-100 ms mean, the trigram index over the walk cache 44-57 ms mean (25-32 ms of it stat-ing every file to prove the index current) after a one-time 1.7 s build, about 170 MB more resident memory (210 MB vs 38 MB), and 2.2 ms vs 1.1 ms on the 181-file tree; whole-file reads of all 18,432 files - std::fs::read on 4 threads 233-342 ms, io_uring batches 217-260 ms, fsio's plain batches 240-476 ms, io_uring 2-11 ms vs 1 ms on the small tree.

options.title: Keep shell-tools' trigram index for find
options.consequences: About 2x faster warm searches on a large tree, 1 ms on a typical one; a 1.7 s stall on the build, about 170 MB per indexed tree in a long-lived daemon, and a stat of every file on every search.

options.title: Keep io_uring and POSIX AIO batched loading
options.consequences: Within noise of parallel std reads on a big tree, slower on a small one; 470 lines of unsafe platform code.

options.title: Use the daemon's walk cache, find scan and outlines
options.consequences: One walk, one scan and one outline per daemon, shared by text and JSON answers; search skips files over 2 MiB and counts matching lines.

entities.decision: The daemon's walk cache, find scan (with its binary-file memory) and outlines serve JSON requests through the Host trait; shell-tools' walk.rs, index.rs (TriIndex), uring.rs, aio.rs, par.rs, batched loading (AFS_BATCH_IO), result cache and tree-sitter grammars were removed. shell-tools keeps the JSON protocol and its rendering, the etag memory (now shared by a daemon's sessions, with a table per session), JSON read with its diff replies, stat and diff_since, which the daemon lacked: its read-again resends a whole reply and its diff is git's. The daemon's text commands keep their own reply dedupe (Sessions), which hashes rendered text; the library's memory tracks file versions so it can skip loading a file and send hunks.
entities.rationale: The walk cache wins clearly (5-9 ms vs 85-145 ms per walk). The index wins about 40 ms per search only on large trees, at a cost in memory and a build stall that a daemon serving many trees for hours pays everywhere; io_uring does not win. One walk and one scan also mean one listing cache and one set of skip rules for every answer.

entities.title: Whole-file reads, not mmap
entities.summary: Files are read into a buffer with read(2); mmap is deliberately not used.
entities.context: The daemon is a long-lived process that reads files other programs may be editing at the same moment; read, stat and diff_since load files in this library.

options.title: mmap
options.consequences: No copy, but truncating a mapped file while it is read raises SIGBUS and kills the process.

options.title: read(2) into a buffer
options.consequences: One copy per file; a file changed mid-read gives stale or partial bytes, which the stamps and the racy window catch, never a crash.

entities.decision: Read whole files with read(2). On Linux, open with O_NOATIME (retried without it when the kernel refuses with EPERM because the caller does not own the file) and hint posix_fadvise(SEQUENTIAL).
entities.rationale: Truncating a mapped file raises SIGBUS and would kill the daemon.
entities.origin: src/macos/shell-tools/README.md, section I/O, before it moved here.

entities.title: Stamps younger than 2 seconds prove nothing
entities.summary: A file's stamp is trusted to mean "unchanged" only once its mtime and ctime are more than 2 seconds older than the moment the stamp was taken.
entities.context: read skips re-reading and re-hashing a file whose stamp (device, inode, size, mtime and ctime in nanoseconds) is unchanged. A file edited twice within one timestamp tick, with the same size, keeps the same stamp.
entities.decision: Ident.racy marks a stamp racy when max(mtime, ctime) + 2 s is later than the time it was taken. A racy stamp never lets read skip loading the file. The daemon's walk cache applies the same rule to its listings.
entities.rationale: The rule git uses for its index: same-tick edits cannot serve stale data.
entities.origin: src/macos/shell-tools/README.md, section Caching, before it moved here.

entities.title: Staleness by re-stat, not file-system events
entities.summary: Trusted file stamps are checked by stat-ing the file on each read; no inotify, fanotify or FSEvents watcher keeps a dirty set.
entities.context: read answers unchanged without loading a file whose stamp still matches the one recorded with its etag.

options.title: Re-stat the file on each read
options.consequences: One stat per read; nothing platform-specific.

options.title: File-system event watchers
options.consequences: Three platform APIs for a saving of one stat per read.

entities.origin: src/macos/shell-tools/README.md, sections Caching and Not implemented, before they moved here.

entities.title: What may change in the JSON request protocol
entities.summary: Agents rely on op and field names and on reply fields such as unchanged, ref, hunks, next_ranges and next_cursor through `zazzle call` and zazzle_call; nothing says which of them may change.
entities.context: The request-protocol contract in src/macos/shell-tools/src/.dev/contracts.json is relied on by coding agents through `zazzle call`, the MCP tool zazzle_call and agents/skills/zazzle/SKILL.md. The merge into the daemon kept the op and field names and already changed some replies (README section Compatibility); the repository states no compatibility policy.

options.title: Additive only
options.consequences: Fields and tools are only added; a rename or removal needs a new name.

options.title: Change freely with the skill
options.consequences: Any change is allowed if the skill and the README change in the same commit; agents with older instructions may break.
